correctness.rationale: Reconstructed dim(XT_n)=sum_j rank(X[1:j,1:j]) and dim(T_n X)=sum_i rank(X[i:n,i:n]) by independent triangular columns/rows. Leading profile is at most min(r,j-1); trailing at least max(r-i+1,0), giving sharp bound. Positive equality forces nonzero first r superdiagonal pivots and zero rows below r; coordinates yield the torus-affine locus. Anti-diagonal-transpose gives negative extremizers. A sequence of nonattacking rook placements moves one coordinate at a time, changing the difference by -1, so every intervening integer occurs. Boundary r=0,n-1 gives zero. New direct exact GF(2) enumeration covered n=2..5 (1098 matrices), including direct product-span ranks and counts; all passed, but finite results are not the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: One-sided principal ideal dimension imbalance is a natural measure of left-right asymmetry in hereditary triangular matrix algebras. The theorem resolves the sharp rank-dependent scale, every possible gap, and the entire equality geometry over arbitrary fields; rank and Jordan type alone cannot distinguish the signed gap.

final_claim: For X strictly upper triangular in T_n(k), rank r, the left/right principal ideal dimension difference exhausts all integers from -r(n-r-1) to +r(n-r-1), and its global maximum absolute value is floor((n-1)^2/4). The positive equality locus is a torus-affine product with count (q-1)^r q^{rn-r(r+3)/2} over F_q; k any field, n>=2.
